title: Rerankers
summary: A reranker rescoring a shortlist with a model that reads query and chunk together. It improves order, not recall: it cannot find chunks the first stage missed.
useIf: The right chunk is usually in the shortlist but not at the top, and you can afford extra latency and cost per query.
avoidIf: The right chunk is not in the candidate set, or the latency budget leaves no room for a second model pass.

explain.md: First-stage retrievers are built for speed over millions of chunks, so they score query and chunk separately. A **cross-encoder** feeds the query and one candidate through a transformer together and outputs a single relevance score, with attention across both. It is more accurate and too slow for a whole corpus, so it rescores only a shortlist, for example 100 candidates [[tr7]]. BEIR found re-ranking and late-interaction models gave the best zero-shot average, at high compute cost [[r11]].

explain.title: Retrieve wide, rerank narrow
explain.alt: A first stage returns many candidates, the top 50 go to the reranker, and a handful of the best go to the model.

head: Family
How it scores
Notes from the sources
rows: Managed ranking inside the search service

Reranks the top 50 only and cannot find new documents. About 2,000 tokens per document feed summarisation, and the summary string is capped at 2,048 tokens (256 before November 2024). `@search.rerankerScore` runs 0 to 4 [[r3]]
`rerank-v4.0-pro` and `rerank-v4.0-fast` take 32k context, `rerank-v3.5` takes 4096 tokens. Results carry `index` and `relevance_score`. YAML strings recommended for structured documents [[r31]]
You control data residency and cost, and you own GPUs and updates [[tr7]]
Prompted model orders a window of candidates
RankGPT found instructed GPT-class models competitive with supervised rerankers. Cost is an extra model call per window [[r13]]
Encodes query and document independently [[tr11]]. Index grows about tenfold, which ColBERTv2 compresses [[r12]]. Not documented in the Azure vector pages read on 2026-10-13

explain.md: **Where reranking pays.** In Anthropic's tests the top-20 retrieval failure rate fell from 5.7% to 3.7% with contextual embeddings and to 2.9% with contextual BM25 added. Adding reranking brought the reduction to 67% [[r26]]. **Where it cannot help.** A relevant chunk at candidate position 80 never reaches an Azure reranker that takes 50, so raise first-stage recall before blaming the ranker.

explain.title: Azure semantic ranker limits that bite
explain.md: `search=*` or an empty search disables it, `orderBy` with semantic returns HTTP 400, and it is billed when `queryType=semantic` and the search string is not empty. Score distributions shift with model updates, so avoid fine cutoffs [[r3]].

whereToUse: After hybrid retrieval, where fused order is rough and the model sees only 5 to 10 chunks
Corpora with many near-duplicate or topically similar chunks, where order matters
Long-form answers where the top chunk must truly answer the question
Systems that return extractive captions or answers directly from the ranker

use: The gold chunk sits in the top 50 but rarely in the top 5
You can afford extra latency per query (author estimate: tens to hundreds of milliseconds, so measure on your data)
A managed option exists in your search service
avoid: Strict latency budgets such as voice, with no spare milliseconds
You need stable absolute scores for thresholds across model updates
flips: Data cannot leave your network: use a self-hosted cross-encoder
Documents are long: check the ranker's input limit, since only a summary or window is read
Query volume is huge: shrink the candidate window or rerank only the hard queries

pitfalls.symptom: The relevant document never appears even with the ranker on
pitfalls.cause: It was outside the top 50 candidates, and the ranker only reorders
pitfalls.fix: Raise first-stage recall: hybrid, query transformation, `k` and `maxTextRecallSize` so they sum to at least 50 [[r2]]

pitfalls.symptom: Abstention rate jumps after a service update
pitfalls.fix: Recalibrate coarse bands on the golden set and monitor score percentiles

scenarios.title: Azure-native stack, order is noisy
scenarios.situation: A hybrid index sits in Azure AI Search. Evaluation shows the gold chunk is in the top 50 for nearly every query but only in the top 5 for about half.
constraints: Data must stay inside the search service boundary
unknowns: Is semantic ranker available in the region and tier?
scenarios.question: What do you add?

options.name: Enable the semantic ranker and set coarse bands for any cutoff
options.why: It fits the in-service data constraint and targets exactly the symptom of good recall with weak order [[r3]].
options.tradeoff: Premium billing, and scores drift with model updates.

options.name: Add an LLM reranker over the top 50
options.tradeoff: Higher latency and cost, and data leaves the service.

options.name: Increase `k` to 200 and send everything to the model
options.why: It floods the context and does not fix order.
options.tradeoff: Fine for a model with a large window when ordering matters little.

flips.if: The gold chunk is often outside the top 50
flips.then: Fix first-stage recall before adding or tuning a ranker.
Use a hosted rerank API or a self-hosted cross-encoder.

scenarios.takeaway: Rerank when the order is bad, not when the shortlist is bad.

scenarios.title: Regulated data, own search engine
scenarios.situation: A bank runs OpenSearch inside its network. Documents cannot go to an external API. Analysts accept a two-second response.
constraints: A small ML platform team exists
scenarios.question: Which reranker?

options.name: Self-hosted cross-encoder over the top 50 to 100
options.why: It keeps data inside the boundary and the latency budget tolerates a model pass [[tr7]].
options.tradeoff: You operate GPUs, evaluate model updates and tune on your data.

options.name: Hosted rerank API
options.why: It sends document text outside the network.
options.tradeoff: Right when residency rules allow a vendor and you want zero operations.

options.name: No reranker, trust the hybrid order
options.tradeoff: Top-5 order may be noisy, which hurts answer quality.

flips.if: The platform team cannot run GPUs
flips.then: Ship without a reranker first and revisit with a vendor approved for the data.

flips.if: The response budget tightens to well under a second
flips.then: Shrink the rerank window to about 20 to 30 candidates or use a smaller distilled cross-encoder.

scenarios.takeaway: Residency often chooses the reranker for you.

scenarios.title: Voice assistant with a tight budget
scenarios.situation: A voice agent must speak within about a second of the end of the question. Retrieval is allotted 250 ms.
unknowns: How precise is first-stage retrieval on a labelled set?
Can the reranker run on a small candidate window?
scenarios.question: How do you handle reranking?

options.name: Measure first-stage precision, and rerank only a small window (for example 20) if it fits the budget
options.why: Cost scales with candidates, so a small window may fit, and the measurement shows whether reranking is needed.
options.tradeoff: A smaller window lowers the chance the gold chunk is included.

options.name: Rerank 100 candidates with an LLM
options.why: An extra model call per window blows the budget [[r13]].
options.tradeoff: Right for offline or asynchronous research workflows.

options.name: Skip reranking permanently
options.tradeoff: Gives up accuracy that might be affordable.

flips.if: The budget grows to a second or more
First-stage precision at 20 is already very high on the golden set
flips.then: Skip the reranker and keep the saved latency, since it would reorder little.

scenarios.takeaway: Candidate window size is the latency dial.

quiz.q: After enabling the Azure semantic ranker, a relevant document still never appears. Debug output shows it at position 74 before reranking. What is the cause?
options: Only the top 50 candidates go to the ranker
The ranker scores it too low
quiz.explain: Position 74 is outside the top 50 that the ranker receives, so it is never rescored. Fix first-stage recall. The other options do not match the evidence.

quiz.q: Match each reranker to its defining property.

pairs.r: Scores query and chunk together with attention across both
Independent encodings with token-level interaction, large index
Prompted model orders a window, extra call per window
Reranks the top 50 and cannot find new documents

quiz.explain: These are the properties each source describes: cross-encoders attend across query and document, ColBERT delays interaction, LLM rerankers add a model call and Azure's ranker only reorders its 50 candidates.

quiz.q: Which is the strongest reason to choose a self-hosted cross-encoder over a hosted rerank API?
options: It removes the need for first-stage recall
Document text must not leave your network
quiz.explain: Residency is the decisive dial. Accuracy depends on the model and data, self-hosting needs compute, and no reranker fixes missing candidates.

flashcards.front: Why can a reranker not fix poor recall?
flashcards.back: It only reorders the candidates it receives. Azure's semantic ranker takes the top 50 and cannot find new documents.
0.00 to 4.00. The distribution shifts with model updates, so use coarse cutoffs only.
A cross-encoder scores query and chunk together, which is accurate but slow. A bi-encoder embeds them separately, which is fast for first-stage search.
